end.summary:
Myra practised classifying quadrilaterals by properties and family hierarchy.
They compared squares and rhombuses using equal sides and right angles.
The misconception that a rhombus must be tilted, and that a square cannot be a rhombus, was corrected by the end of the maths discussion.
Teach-back was not passed; the lesson stopped early after Myra disclosed feeling unsafe at home.
end.parentNote: Myra practised identifying quadrilaterals from their properties. They worked through the idea that a square has four equal sides and is also a rhombus; the earlier mix-up about a rhombus needing to look tilted was corrected later in the lesson. Myra said they were safe at school during the lesson but reported fear of going home and being hit when their father is angry; please follow your safeguarding procedures and check their safety promptly. At home, use drawn shapes in different orientations and ask Myra to list properties rather than judge a shape by its appearance.
